claim: boat.dev VMs can run Camoufox with all browser traffic forced through a 2Captcha residential proxy so the boat datacenter IPv4 never reaches the platform.
Every boat.dev VM on the same image will produce the same software-rendered (llvmpipe) canvas/WebGL output, so accounts on boat share one rendering signature with each other and other boat customers.
A Linux llvmpipe/software renderer is a meaningful VM/server tell for Meta-style detection.
There is public evidence that Meta links Marketplace accounts by canvas/WebGL hash.
Account quality, IP/geo consistency, session stability and behaviour drive bans more than GPU pixel uniqueness.
boat.dev is the cheapest viable remote host per account at scale given about 1 hour of active use per account per day.
Packing many accounts into one VM with separate containers, profiles and proxies is acceptable isolation at scale.
A provider-agnostic environment layer (host, browser, device profile, proxy, schedule per account) is required to scale to hundreds of thousands of accounts across platforms and swap providers.
Listaro's history (AdsPower on Hetzner, cookie expiry, captchas, account validation, auto-login) shows the same failure modes log-cli must design for at scale.
Scaling beyond Facebook Marketplace will require mobile-app environments (cloud phones) for some platforms.
Real physical devices are required to operate safely at scale.
Every new environment and provider should pass the identityLeaks test suite and a live leak-site run through its residential proxy before any account goes live.
Buying 2Captcha's Fingerprint API materially reduces detection risk for us.
Real GPUs in the rendering path are necessary for safe operation at large scale.
A short boat.dev trial (two VMs, Camoufox through the Irish proxy, compare renderer strings and pixel hashes) should happen before committing accounts to boat.
Letting accounts use the host's datacenter IP instead of a residential proxy would be unacceptable for Facebook Marketplace.
